newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies finish lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies finish lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were choppy late and closed mixed as uncertainty grew over the direction of cash hog prices while pork bellies fell in line with another loss in cash belly prices, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.125 cent per lb lower to 0.450 higher with February and April ending up 0.025 with April at 74.800 cents. Pork bellies finished 0.800 to 0.150 cent lower with March off most at 76.450 cent.
Firmer-than-expected cash hog markets early Wednesday prompted initial short-covering support, but those prices weakened, sparking uneven futures trade into the close.

Futures broke late as commercial selling touched off sell stops, but prices held technical support despite an overall bearish technical picture to again rally for gains. Local short covering and buying by Cargill Investor Services boosted prices to net gains before selling by Rand Financials and LFG again provided pressure at the closing bell, they said.
"There's a lot of uncertainty in the market," said Julia Bussie, analyst for AG Edwards.
Bussie noted that longs are saying hog marketings are current while shorts still expect storm-backed-up numbers to be marketed and packers don't want them anyway.
Packers are cutting back on kills due to continued poor cutout margins, traders said.

The cutback in kills underpinned pork belly futures, but prices fell around midday when USDA again reported cash belly prices dipped another $1 per cwt to $69, the lowest level in two weeks. Belly futures had rallied from early losses on short covering and bargain hunting but weakened again when cash eased further, they said.
An increase in deliverable stocks reported in the storage report and a small in-movement versus an out-movement last year sparked the early weakness, they added.

CME reported a net in-movement of 24,000 lbs last week in the out-of-town report. This compared with early trade estimates of unchanged to in 500,000 lbs, but deliverable stocks rose to 7.2 million from 6.28 million lbs.
Rand notably sold February and March while E.D.&F. Man spread long May/short February, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission house bought June 76 and 78 puts, pit sources added.
